title: Forge Workshop Kit: six practical workflows
capture_policy: Actual browser captures. Playback follows capture timestamps; final-frame holds provide reading time. No new workshop model or training execution.

shots.label: Public workshop library
shots.description: The six workshop cards
narration: We built these workshops for engineers who want to understand the work around an AI application after its first demo succeeds.
A refund agent can finish an API call and leave the account wrong. A forecast can have a score nobody can reproduce. Two coding agents can finish assignments whose parts disagree.

shots.label: Published learning Report
shots.description: The published Report introduction
narration: The Reports introduce each problem through a worked example, with code and recorded results.
You can read the explanation first, then try the same exercise in your own project.

shots.label: Recorded account change
shots.description: The complete account comparison in the published Report
narration: The customer needs one duplicate payment refunded. The account comparison shows whether the agent changed only that payment.

shots.label: Copy, import or run locally
shots.description: The public notebook start page and setup instructions
narration: Each start page links the Forge template, the current notebook download, and laptop instructions. Copy the template into your own project and check access.
Use the download if hosted notebooks are unavailable to your account. Your inference allowance starts at eight dollars; compute and ARIA usage are separate.

shots.label: Facilitator instructions
shots.description: The running guide
narration: The running guide covers demos and full sessions. Code, free checks, run buttons, and results stay together. Opening saved work starts no training or inference.

chapters.title: Pending: inspect and change an agent

shots.label: Interactive teaching guide
shots.description: The invoice dispatch and observation sequence
narration: Pending handles office billing and account access. A customer needs a duplicate charge refunded.
Participants write an invoice tool, dispatch an action, and append its returned observation to the next model request. The drawing follows that invoice through each operation.

shots.label: Saved execution in Agent Lens
shots.description: Actual arguments and returned account data
narration: In Agent Lens, inspect the actual arguments, returned result, timing, and next action. The account check tests the customer outcome.
A committed write can lose its response. Reusing the operation ID prevents a duplicate membership.
Participants compare manual and agent-written harness changes on matching cases. The recorded final pass count tied, despite different tool behavior.

shots.label: Real observations; teaching view
shots.description: One forecast window and its target
narration: Solar is a lab preparing its weekly forecast review with real GOES measurements and AIA images.
Follow one timestamp through the history window and separate future target. Persistence copies the latest reading forward, giving each trained model a baseline to beat.

shots.label: Saved training run
shots.description: Six configurations, validation error and runtime
narration: Train small models and inspect their loss curves. A Sweep compares six existing configurations.
Then a research agent proposes image-model edits. Review the diffs, train candidates, and compare. The language model stays fixed while forecasting weights train.

shots.label: Solar selected source · exact artifact
shots.description: The exact source saved with the selected Solar image model
narration: Artifacts preserve the tested source, settings, weights, and predictions. The unsuccessful GOES recipe and mixed image results stay visible, so participants can investigate both.

shots.label: Controlled release defect
shots.description: The same probability columns with different intent mappings
narration: Routing follows a banking support queue. A missing card needs a different workflow from a card that does not work.
This controlled release defect reorders intent names without moving probability columns. A confident score now selects the wrong queue.
Participants write a regression check, repair the loader, and restore a previous version. The classifier itself has not changed.

shots.label: Saved aligned requests
shots.description: Matching requests and evaluated predictions
narration: Using Banking77, fit a baseline, inspect validation mistakes, and test another text representation.

EvalTables aligns requests, predictions, labels, and errors across versions. Runs compare models. Artifacts preserve preprocessing, intent order, and the classifier. The release is a notebook batch predictor.

shots.label: Real PCB features; worked calculation
shots.description: One patch and its normal reference
narration: Inspection checks circuit boards before shipping, using real VisA photographs. Investigate a missed defect before replacing whole-image features with local patches.
This calculation finds one patch's closest normal reference. Its distance becomes a feature, not a causal explanation. Supplied defect masks help inspection, but never enter the classifier.

shots.label: Saved board predictions
shots.description: Actual board images, scores and labels
narration: EvalTables shows boards beside scores and labels. Inspect a recovered miss and a new mistake, then compare active and random review with equal labeling budgets.
Artifacts retain the feature code, reference bank, classifier, and threshold. More labels helping does not establish a better selection method.

shots.label: Deterministic coordination exercise
shots.description: The claim race and atomic repair
narration: Transit uses two coding agents to build a departure board from a historical MBTA schedule.
Implement dependencies, atomic claims, ownership, and integration. Two workers must not claim the same task.
Submitted, tested, and integrated are separate states. Finished assignments still need combined application checks.

shots.label: Saved R5 acceptance comparison
shots.description: Matching solo and team acceptance cases
narration: On matching cases, the team failed two checks that the solo build passed. Twenty-four-oh-eight belongs to the original service day, making integration concrete.
Agent Lens records edits, tests, and handoffs; Artifacts preserve releases. Fresh workers then run with and without a verified lesson. The recorded memory comparison found no advantage.

shots.label: Simulated booking; controlled example
shots.description: Original, incomplete and preserved itineraries
narration: Airline follows a passenger changing part of a round trip, using simulated benchmark bookings.
The API replaces the whole itinerary. Sending only the changed outbound flight can remove the return.
Compare the original, incomplete, and preserved itineraries. A successful API call can leave the booking wrong.

shots.label: Saved airline conversation
shots.description: A recoverable tool timeout and the passenger request
narration: Inspect this recoverable timeout, then review the turn before calibrating a tag. Agent Lens covers Conversations, Insights, Tags, and Alignment.
Reviewed incidents become regression cases, and EvalTables compares repairs. Monitor agreement and agent correctness remain separate.
The recorded agent passed; the itinerary defect is controlled. Native Alignment and prepared Insights still need qualification. Missing judgments remain unavailable.

chapters.title: ARIA: investigate a result, then verify a claim

shots.label: Shared notebook card; saved response
shots.description: The actual shared ARIA controls with a restored response
narration: Explain a result before asking ARIA. Start ARIA investigation sends your question and selected records.
The notebook saves the conversation. Check ARIA response retrieves the answer. Opening the notebook sends nothing.

shots.label: Existing ARIA conversation; analysis only
shots.description: The actual ARIA answer to a development question
narration: Open ARIA conversation continues the discussion in Forge. Check what the records support.
ARIA neither scores results nor approves repairs. Organization settings govern its usage, outside the notebook allowance.

shots.label: Verify the cited record
shots.description: The cited execution artifact opened from the answer
narration: Open one cited record. Mark the claim supported, disputed, or unresolved. The recorded fallback teaches the same check.

chapters.title: Use the material and measure the entry path

shots.label: How to run a workshop
shots.description: Setup, timing and fallbacks
narration: Each deck has a running guide for preparation, timing, recorded fallbacks, and participant progress.
Full sessions remain technical previews while external-account and participant rehearsals are outstanding.
For a customer conversation, choose the closest problem. A five-minute investigation often explains more than a product tour. The guide names what to show and what to inspect.

shots.label: External attribution; no participant identity
shots.description: Public entry link and tracking explanation
narration: External video, Slack, and workshop QR links have distinct UTM.io tags. Reusing a link combines those entry paths. Coworkers use the direct address.
Visits do not measure notebook copies or completion; previews and repeat visits affect counts.

shots.label: Read or try one exercise
shots.description: Workshop entry points
narration: Read a Report, open a deck, or follow the notebook instructions. Participant checkpoints feed the facilitator roster. Missing updates mean unknown.
Anonymous visits remain separate from participant identities. Also ask pilot participants where they got stuck and what helped.

shots.label: Public workshop library
shots.description: Choose a relevant workshop
narration: Leave with a result you can explain and reproduce. Notebooks hold code. Agent Lens shows behavior. Runs and Sweeps compare experiments. Artifacts preserve files. EvalTables aligns cases. Reports explain the conclusion.

shots.label: Copy, import or run locally
shots.description: The public notebook start page and setup instructions
narration: Choose a problem your team faces. Read its Report, try a demo, or copy or download the notebook.
Follow the linked running instructions, and tell us what needs improvement.
